text_content: the blueprint for flood control masterplan is ready the recent post by fb page more of davao has reignited an important conversation-davao city's flooding problem is not due to the absence of a plan in fact one already exists the japan international cooperation agency jica in partnership with the department of public works and highways dpwh completed the project for master plan and feasibility study on flood control and drainage in davao city in july 2023 after several years of technical studies and consultations the project itself commenced in november 2018 following the signing of the record of discussions in april 2018 between jica and the philippine government the completed master plan is comprehensive it covers the davao matina and talomo river basins and recommends a combination of structural measures including river dredging cut-off channels retarding ponds retarding basins and drainage improvements to significantly reduce flood risks in the city these are not theoretical concepts they are the product of years of hydrological studies engineering surveys and technical analysis by filipino and japanese experts this is why the public deserves to know one thing what is the current status of implementation large official development assistance oda infrastructure projects commonly undergo additional stages that include financing arrangements detailed engineering environmental compliance right-of-way acquisition and government approvals before actual construction begins that does not diminish the urgency every flooding incident reminds us that studies alone cannot protect lives master plans only become meaningful once construction begins the engineering has already been completed the science has already been established the blueprint already exists the next chapter should no longer be about producing another report it should be about turning years of planning into flood control infrastructure that protects communities businesses and lives because when it comes to flooding what davaoeños need most is not another promise-they need progress backed by action

text_content: the hostage blueprint jica masterplan for davao city what if i told you that a blueprint to stop the flooding in davao city is already finished it was designed by some of the best engineers in the world printed and is currently sitting on a desk in manila here is the truth about the jica master plan the political war currently holding it hostage and what our local government unit lgu is doing to keep our heads above water while we wait the real solution the jica master plan back in 2018 the philippine government partnered with the japan international cooperation agency jica to solve our city's flooding instead of just building basic concrete walls which easily overflow the japanese and local engineers designed a massive city-wide system the core of the plan involves digging massive retarding basins giant empty catch-ponds built in the uplands when a storm hits millions of gallons of water would flow into these basins and be held there safely trapping the water before it ever reaches barangays like ma-a matina and talomo it is brilliant it is proven and it is ready but just look at the timeline of how it got stuck in politics here is the timeline april 2019 the study begins the philippine government and the japan international cooperation agency jica sign an agreement to create a long-term multi-basin master plan 2018-2022 why wasn't it built under duterte a common question is why this wasn't funded during former president rodrigo duterte's term the answer is engineering reality the japanese engineers were still studying our rivers you cannot fund or construct a mega-project when the architects haven't finished the blueprints july 2023 the blueprint is finished jica officially completes the master plan instead of basic walls it proposes php 41.7 billion to build massive retarding basins giant empty bowls upstream to catch and hold storm water before it hits our urban barangays august 9 2024 vp sara calls out the missing budget vice president sara duterte issues a strong public statement pointing out the lack of government action she calls out the current administration for refusing to fund the finalized master plan questioning if the budget is being intentionally withheld simply because the sitting mayor is a duterte baka naman may alinlangan pa hinggil dito dahil duterte ang mayor at mas mamarapatin nilang gibain na lang she stated 2025 present still waiting for funds despite the blueprint being ready for over two years the national government has still not released the funding needed to actually build it bureaucracy or sabotage while politicians debate whether the delay is just standard government red tape for a foreign loan or a deliberate political attack to damage the duterte family ordinary davaoeños are the collateral damage we are the ones sweeping mud out of our homes the ultimate solution to our flooding is being treated as a political football what is the lgu doing while we wait the davao city local government cannot afford a php 41.7 billion mega-project on its own they cannot single-handedly buy multi-hectare lands to build giant retarding ponds without national funding however they are not just sitting around waiting for our government without the big blueprint the lgu is focusing heavily on immediate urban drainage nature-based mitigation and survival here is what the city is doing right now aggressive drainage and inlet upgrades the city engineer's office ceo and task force drainage are continuously ripping up flood-prone choke points in 2025 alone they funded five new major inlet projects to help water subside faster on critical roads like diversion road fronting panacan cemetery quezon boulevard and cabantian-bunawan preventing blockages the city's ancillary services unit asu is conducting aggressive year-round desilting and garbage clearing of these new drainage systems so the street-level water actually has somewhere to go smart early warning systems if the lgu cannot completely stop the water they focus on keeping people alive davao city relies heavily on its high-definition river cameras monitoring the talomo matina and davao rivers 24/7 this real-time data triggers sirens and preemptive evacuations long before the flood hits living rooms wetlands protection the city is pushing for stricter zoning laws to protect remaining natural wetlands and text_content: davao's flood defenses explained how retarding ponds cut-off channels and dredging work when millions of cubic meters of water pour down from upstream mountain catchments into the davao talomo and matina river basins how do we protect our communities from being submerged the insights and data shared here are not my own-they are drawn directly from the official dpwh-jica flood control master plan in part 1 we broke down why different neighborhoods face completely different flood risks today in part 2 we take a deep dive into the 4 major hard engineering solutions designed under this master plan to store accelerate and safely convey extreme 100 year flood waters out to sea 1 priority retarding ponds temporary storage upstream affected downstream areas callawa mandug waan tigatto ma-a bucana talomo proper matina crossing and matina aplaya how it works think of these as massive engineered overflow reservoirs during heavy storms river channels quickly fill up retarding ponds capture the peak flood surge upstream holding the excess water back until river levels safely drop the engineering specs davao river rp 08 callawa new valencia 3.5 million m3 capacity davao river rp 09 upper callawa bend 2.1 million m3 capacity davao river rp 11 mandug new carmen 4.8 million m3 capacity talomo river basin multi-site retention ponds covering approximately 4.8 million m2 to absorb excess volume before it hits downtown matina river basin a network of 12 critical offline/online ponds ponds 8-10 13-18 23-25 strategically distributed to capture and cut peak flood discharge by 200 m3 s combined impact over 10.4 million cubic meters of temporary flood storage for the davao river alone plus massive secondary retention across talomo and matina-the equivalent of thousands of olympic-sized swimming pools held back from swamping the city 2 cut-off channels coc straightening extreme river bends affected areas callawa new valencia ma-a riverfront area plus localized bottlenecks in matina and talomo how it works natural winding river loops slow down water velocity forcing floodwaters to pile up and breach their banks cut-off channels construct straight bypass canals directly across narrow meander necks the engineering specs the 1.8 km callawa cut-off channel speeds up water flow dramatically dropping peak flood levels upstream and relieving severe hydraulic pressure on tight river bends additionally short-term cut-off channel works are programmed for the winding sections of the matina and talomo rivers to prevent backwater piling and safely accelerate flow toward the coast 3 channel widening and dredging reclaiming river capacity affected areas ma-a tigatto bankerohan barangay 19 bucana matina crossing and talomo urban center how it works decades of mountain erosion have washed tons of silt onto the riverbed choking its flow capacity while dense urban build-up has dangerously narrowed the natural waterways the engineering specs deep channel dredging and excavation along critical downstream reaches of the davao river lower the riverbed profile-expanding cross-sectional flow area so the river can carry higher discharge volumes in the matina river the channel will be physically widened by an average of 6 meters 3m on each bank and 6 restrictive hydraulic bottleneck bridges will be replaced this massive upgrade will more than double matina's flow capacity from a dangerous 150 m3 s up to a safe 350 m3 s 4 floodwalls dikes and revetments wall-to-wall protection affected areas densely populated urban barangays along the davao talomo and matina river corridors how it works where urban density prevents widening the river lateral structures contain the water within the channel raised concrete dikes prevent overflow while heavy reinforced concrete revetments absorb raging currents to prevent riverbank collapse the engineering specs alongside the massive dikes for the main davao river and drainage integration at the macarthur highway corridor in talomo the highly vulnerable matina river urban stretch will receive heavy reinforcements new concrete floodwalls here will average 2.6 meters high-reaching up to a towering 5.4 meters in critical spots including freeboard to securely contain the raging 100 year flood volumes the takeaway system integration is key no single dike or dredging project can solve davao city's flood challenges alone retarding ponds hold back the surge upstream cut-off channels speed up flow past tight meanders and downstream widening dredging and dikes safely guide the water text_content: it was more than a punch by truth stream the rain did not arrive with a warning loud enough to stir panic it came like countless other rainy nights in davao city steady familiar almost ordinary dabawenyos tucked their children into bed believing morning would come as it always had but somewhere in the darkness the waters were already gathering strength silently preparing to rewrite the lives of an entire community before dawn broke on june 30 2011 matina pangi had become the epicenter of one of davao city's deadliest flash floods in a matter of minutes homes were swallowed by a raging torrent parents desperately searched for their children neighbors risked their own lives to save strangers when the floodwaters finally receded they left behind more than shattered houses and mud-covered streets they left empty cradles unfinished dreams and a city mourning the loss of more than thirty lives most of them children mayor inday sara duterte then only 33 years old and herself a young mother woke up to a city devastated by tragedy one infant was never found entire families were caught in total darkness as floodwaters engulfed their homes some survived only by climbing trees while others escaped to the matina pangi bridge carrying nothing but the clothes on their backs and the cellphones they managed to save as daylight broke the full extent of the catastrophe emerged lifeless bodies waiting to be recovered children still missing families desperately searching for loved ones and survivors left with nothing but mud where their homes once stood for mayor sara there was no time to grieve she immediately led relief operations visited evacuation centers comforted bereaved families and coordinated rescue and emergency response efforts sleep and rest had to wait yet before the city could even begin to recover from one tragedy another crisis erupted a court-ordered demolition in agdao was set to proceed despite the city's standing policy that no demolition should take place unless affected residents had first been relocated knowing the emotional state of the people after the flash flood mayor sara appealed to the court sheriff for just one or two hours so she could personally speak with the residents her request was neither unreasonable nor defiant she simply wanted to prevent panic violence and the possibility of more people getting hurt barely twenty-four hours had passed since more than thirty lives most of them children had been lost she did not want another tragedy unfolding in another part of the city her plea was ignored while she was still in matina attending to flood victims she learned that the demolition had already begun she rushed to agdao wearing a light blue shirt and her signature short hair where television cameras were already rolling she motioned for the sheriff to come closer seconds later she threw the punch that would become one of the most replayed political images in recent philippine history across the country many saw only a mayor punching a court officer what many never saw was the context he grief exhaustion and emotional weight of the previous twenty-four hours they did not see the flood victims she had just come from the parents searching for missing children or the families she had spent the day consoling the image of the punch became the story while everything that led to it slowly faded from public memory mayor sara later ensured that the sheriff received medical treatment publicly expressed regret over what had happened and in time both of them moved on from the incident fifteen years later however that single moment was once again thrust into the national spotlight during the impeachment proceedings against vice president sara duterte where prosecutors cited it as evidence of an alleged pattern of violent behavior for many dabawenyos though the hearing revived a different memory they remembered the flood before they remembered the punch they remembered the children who died the families who lost everything and the young mayor who spent every waking hour responding to one of the darkest days in the city's history before rushing to stop what she believed could become another human tragedy as old footage resurfaced so did countless personal stories from dabawenyos whose admiration for the dutertes had been shaped not by political slogans but by lived experience whether one agrees with sara duterte's actions that day or not history is rarely captured in a single frame sometimes what appears to be a single punch is only the final chapter of a much longer story one written in floodwaters grief impossible decisions and a leader's fierce determination to stand with her people perhaps that is why fifteen years later dabawenyos continue to tell the story differently they remember not only the punch they remember everything that came before it vp sara duterte impeachment trial vpsaraimpeach

at first baha sa davao was just another joke a punchline in the comments a little teasing between sides something to laugh at because sometimes humor is how we make sense of the things we cannot control but somewhere between the jokes and the reposts the flood stopped being something we were watching from a screen people started posting their homes underwater their streets turned into rivers their belongings floating away families looking for a way out people asking for help and suddenly it wasn't funny anymore because behind every meme is a person behind every flooded street is a home behind every viral post is someone wondering what they'll have left when the water goes down at this point it doesn't matter who started the teasing it doesn't matter which side you're on it doesn't matter what political belief you hold people are hurting and that should matter more than being right there will always be time for arguments debates and jokes but right now let's choose to be human first if you can help help if you can share verified calls for assistance share them if you can check on someone check on them suffering should never be a punchline
